title: Claude Campus Ambassador Program 2026 – Paid Student Opportunities with Anthropic

title: DAAD University Summer Courses Scholarship 2027: Funded 4-Week German Language Programme With Accommodation, €475 Allowance and Travel Support
summary: Applications are open for the DAAD University Summer Courses offered in Germany for Foreign Students and Graduates , an international scholarship programme that enables eligible university students to spend four intensive weeks studying German language and regional studies at participating higher education institutions in Germany. The programme is administered by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) and funded by Germany’s Federal Foreign Office. Its central objective is to help international students deepen their knowledge of German as a general and technical language while expanding their understanding of German society, culture and regional studies. For the upcoming cycle, applications are accepted from: 1 September 2026 until: 30 October 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time The funded courses themselves take place between June and September 2027 . Courses last four weeks, normally operate no more than five days per week and provide at least 25 teaching hours per week . They are taught entirely in German and must be attended physically in Germany; remote participation is not permitted. The scholarship package includes: Full coverage of the selected language course costs Accommodation arranged by the course provider for the duration of the course A one-time allowance of €475 A country-specific travel allowance for applicants from selected countries Health insurance Accident insurance Personal liability insurance The accommodation is normally provided in a single room , which may be located in a student residence, shared apartment or private household. The programme is open across academic disciplines. Students do not need to be studying German, linguistics or another humanities subject. Eligible applicants may come from fields ranging from engineering and medicine to social sciences, law, arts, natural sciences and economics. However, several important eligibility conditions apply. Applicants must be enrolled at an eligible university outside Germany, must remain enrolled throughout the scholarship period, must have sufficient German-language knowledge, and undergraduate students must have completed at least two years of university study by the beginning of the funded course. Below is a detailed guide to the DAAD University Summer Courses Scholarship 2027 , including funding, eligibility, German-language requirements, application documents, selection criteria, course choice and the application process. About the DAAD University Summer Courses Programme The programme is officially known as: University Summer Courses offered in Germany for Foreign Students and Graduates and is commonly associated with the German abbreviation HSK , referring to university summer language courses. Unlike a full Bachelor s, Master s or doctoral scholarship, this programme funds a short, intensive study period in Germany . Its purpose is specifically to help participants improve: General German Technical or subject-specific German Knowledge of German society Understanding of German culture Knowledge of regional studies Ability to communicate in academic and professional environments The programme therefore combines language development with direct exposure to Germany. Participants do not simply complete an online German course from their home countries. They travel to Germany and study in person at a participating course provider. What Can Be Studied? Funding is available for participation in: German language courses Cultural and regional studies courses Technical and specialized language courses The precise courses available vary according to the participating German universities and course providers. DAAD publishes a dedicated course list containing information such as: Host institution Course dates Required language level Course focus Subject specialization Location Applicants should review the course list before completing their scholarship application. The scholarship application requires candidates to indicate three preferred courses , although these preferences do not guarantee placement in one of the three choices. Courses Are Conducted Entirely in German One of the most important conditions is that: Courses are taught exclusively in German. This is not a beginner programme designed for candidates with no knowledge of German. Applicants need sufficient German-language ability to: Follow lessons Understand instructors Participate in discussions Complete group work Engage meaningfully with course activities Proof of German proficiency must therefore be submitted with the application. In-Person Participation Is Mandatory The programme takes place: Exclusively in person in Germany. DAAD explicitly states that: Remote participation is not possible. Applicants should therefore be ready to travel to Germany and remain there for the full duration of their assigned course. This physical immersion is an important part of the programme because students develop their German not only through classroom study but also through everyday interaction and cultural exposure. Duration of the DAAD Summer Course Scholarship Each funded course lasts: Four weeks The programme normally involves: Maximum five teaching days per week At least 25 teaching hours per week This means participants may complete at least approximately: 100 teaching hours during the four-week period. The scholarship cannot be extended beyond the approved course period. When Do the Courses Take Place? University Summer Courses funded under the programme take place between: June and September For applicants submitting during the September–October 2026 application window, the relevant courses are therefore expected to take place during summer 2027 . Exact dates depend on the course selected and the host institution. Applicants should consult the DAAD course list because different universities may run their programmes at different times within this summer period. Scholarship Benefits The DAAD package contains several significant forms of financial and practical support. 1. Language Course Fees DAAD covers the: Cost of the funded language course. This means scholarship recipients do not need to pay the normal tuition or participation fee for their assigned course. 2. Accommodation Is Provided The course provider arranges accommodation for the scholarship holder during the programme. Accommodation is provided in a: Single room and may be located in settings such as: Student dormitory Shared apartment Private household This is a particularly useful component of the scholarship because students do not need to independently find short-term accommodation in Germany for the four-week programme. 3. €475 One-Time Allowance Scholarship recipients receive a: One-time allowance of €475. This allowance can help with personal costs associated with participation. It is important to understand how it is paid. DAAD does not transfer the €475 allowance abroad before the programme begins . Instead, DAAD transfers the relevant funds to the course provider, which distributes the allowance to scholarship recipients in Germany. 4. Country-Specific Travel Allowance Applicants from selected countries may also receive a: Country-specific travel allowance. The exact value is determined according to the applicant s eligible country and DAAD s applicable travel allowance schedule. Applicants should not assume that every participant receives the same amount. It is also important not to describe the programme as providing universal full airfare reimbursement. DAAD describes this component as a country-specific allowance for selected countries , rather than guaranteeing reimbursement of every travel expense. As with the €475 allowance, applicable travel support is distributed through the course provider on site rather than transferred abroad before the scholarship begins. 5. Health Insurance The scholarship includes: Health insurance benefits during the funded period. This provides important protection for international students temporarily studying in Germany. 6. Accident Insurance The scholarship also includes: Accident insurance for scholarship holders during the programme period. 7. Personal Liability Insurance Participants additionally receive: Personal liability insurance benefits. Taken together, these insurance components provide a broader support package than a simple course-fee waiver. Is This a Fully Funded Scholarship? The programme provides substantial funding, but it is best described as a: Funded short-term scholarship rather than automatically calling it completely cost-free. DAAD covers: Course fees Accommodation €475 allowance Insurance Travel support for selected countries However, applicants should still budget carefully for personal expenses that may exceed the provided allowance. The programme description does not state that every possible expense—such as all meals, all local transport, visa expenses or every euro of international airfare—is universally reimbursed. Who Can Apply? The current DAAD call states that applications are open to: Undergraduate students Master s students from: All academic disciplines. Despite the programme title referring to “Foreign Students and Graduates,” the current live eligibility conditions require applicants to be enrolled at a university at the time of application and throughout the scholarship period . Applicants should therefore follow the current country-specific DAAD scholarship database requirements rather than assuming that anyone who has already graduated and is no longer enrolled automatically qualifies. Undergraduate Eligibility Bachelor s or equivalent undergraduate students can apply. However, they must have completed at least: Two academic years of university study by the time the funded course begins. For example, a student who applies in October 2026 may qualify if they will have completed two full academic years by summer 2027. Master s Students Students enrolled in Master s programmes may also apply. The programme is not restricted to particular Master s disciplines. Candidates may come from subjects including: International relations Engineering Computer science Economics Law Medicine Languages Sociology Political science Natural sciences Arts Business Agriculture Environmental sciences Other recognised fields The central requirement is not the applicant s major but their overall eligibility and motivation for improving their German. Applicants Must Be Enrolled Outside Germany Applicants must be enrolled at a university in one of DAAD s eligible programme countries: Outside Germany both: At the time of application During the entire scholarship period This programme is therefore not designed to fund students who are already studying at a German university as their normal degree institution. Minimum Age Scholarship holders must be: At least 18 years old when the language course begins. The published call does not state a general maximum age limit. Scholarship Can Only Be Used Once DAAD states that funding under this programme can be claimed: Only once. Previous recipients of the same University Summer Courses scholarship should therefore check their eligibility carefully before attempting another application. German-Language Requirement Applicants must demonstrate that they can: Follow lectures in German Participate in German-language group work German knowledge must be documented at the time of application. The precise minimum level may depend on the country-specific version of the scholarship call. DAAD s current country-specific database results show different thresholds in some cases, so applicants should select their own country in the scholarship database and follow the requirement displayed for them rather than relying on a universal minimum level. Accepted German-Language Certificates DAAD lists accepted certificates including: onSET-Deutsch TestDaF Goethe-Institut Zertifikat DSD DSH telc Deutsch ÖSD-Zertifikat Baccalaureate certificate for specialized language courses where applicable Some country-specific calls may also accept the DAAD Language Certificate German under specified conditions. How Recent Must the Language Certificate Be? Generally, the German certificate must not be older than: One year at the time of application. This rule also applies to DSH. However, certificates demonstrating at least: B2, or TDN4 in all TestDaF components may be up to: Two years old. Applicants should therefore check the date of their language test well before beginning the application. Academic Discipline Requirements One major advantage of the programme is that it is not restricted to German Studies students. The DAAD scholarship database lists eligible academic fields across the full disciplinary spectrum, including: Languages and Cultural Studies Law Economics Social Sciences Mathematics Natural Sciences Human Medicine Veterinary Medicine Agriculture Forestry Nutrition Ecology Engineering Art Music Sport This makes the scholarship potentially valuable to students who need German for: Future postgraduate study Research Professional careers International cooperation Academic exchange Technical work Selection Process Applications are reviewed by a: Selection committee rather than being awarded automatically to all eligible candidates. Two principal selection considerations are highlighted by DAAD: Previous academic achievements A convincing motivation letter explaining the chosen programme and future academic plans Meeting the minimum eligibility conditions therefore does not guarantee selection. Academic Achievement Applicants should demonstrate solid performance in their university studies. DAAD requests academic records covering recent university examinations. The selection committee can use these records to assess: Academic consistency Performance Study progress Preparation for the scholarship Applicants should provide complete records rather than selecting only their strongest grades. Motivation Letter A convincing: Letter of motivation is one of the central selection criteria. The motivation letter should explain why the applicant wants to improve their German and how the summer course relates to their: Academic degree Future postgraduate plans Research interests Professional plans Engagement with Germany Academic development A generic statement such as “I like German culture and want to improve my language skills” is unlikely to communicate the same level of purpose as a detailed explanation connecting German proficiency with future academic objectives. Application Documents A complete application requires several documents. 1. Online Application Form Applicants must complete the official: DAAD online application form. The application is submitted through the DAAD portal. 2. Curriculum Vitae Applicants need a: Complete CV in tabular form. The general DAAD call requests the CV in German. Some country-specific rules may provide limited language exceptions, so applicants should follow the instructions displayed for their own country. 3. Motivation Letter Applicants must provide a: Letter of motivation normally in German. The letter should present a clear connection among: Current studies German-language development Course choice Future academic plans 4. University Transcripts Applicants need transcripts covering: University examinations taken during the previous two years including individual grades. If the documents are not already in German or English, a: German translation, or English translation must be included. If a student has been enrolled for less than two years and therefore cannot provide two full years of records, they should provide evidence of academic achievements from their current period of study. 5. School-Leaving Certificate for Undergraduate Applicants Bachelor s-level applicants must also submit their: School-leaving certificate with grades. A German or English translation should be included where necessary. 6. Previous Degree for Postgraduate Students Applicants already studying at postgraduate level should provide their: Most recent university degree certificate including final grades. 7. German-Language Certificate Applicants must upload proof of their German-language proficiency. If necessary, the certificate should be accompanied by a: German translation, or English translation as appropriate. 8. Additional Supporting Documents Candidates may also upload other documents they consider relevant. Examples provided by DAAD include: Internship certificates Employment certificates Applicants should use this option strategically. Additional material should strengthen the case for the scholarship rather than overwhelm the application with unrelated documents. Do Documents Need to Be Certified? At the initial application stage, DAAD states that: Certificates Transcripts Attestations Translations may be submitted in: Uncertified form. However, DAAD reserves the right to request certified copies later. Applicants should therefore retain access to official originals. Incomplete Applications Are Not Considered DAAD makes clear that all required documents must be uploaded by the deadline. Incomplete applications: Cannot be considered in the further selection process. Candidates should therefore avoid submitting at the last moment. Choosing Three Preferred Courses The application asks candidates to identify: Three course preferences. DAAD attempts to take these choices into consideration when placing scholarship holders. However, capacity is limited. DAAD reserves the right to place a successful scholarship recipient in: A different course if the preferred courses are full or placement requirements make another course more appropriate. Course Preferences Cannot Be Changed Later Once the application has been received: Course preferences cannot be changed. Applicants also cannot simply switch to another course after receiving their placement. Candidates should therefore research their three selections carefully before submitting. Consider: Course level Location Dates Specialization Academic relevance Language requirements Step-by-Step Application Process Step 1: Confirm Your Country and Status Go to the DAAD scholarship database and select: Your country Your student status The programme is restricted to specified countries, and requirements can differ depending on the applicant s country. Step 2: Check Your Eligibility Confirm that you: Are enrolled at an eligible university outside Germany Will remain enrolled during the scholarship period Meet the academic-stage requirement Will be at least 18 when the course starts Meet the applicable German-language requirement Have not previously received this scholarship Step 3: Review the Course List Study the available University Summer Courses and identify three suitable choices. Consider which course best supports your: German level Academic specialization Future study Career plans Step 4: Register in the DAAD Portal Applicants must create or access an account in the: DAAD application portal. DAAD advises that its portal has limited functionality on mobile devices and recommends using a desktop computer. Step 5: Complete the Online Form Enter all required information and download or complete the relevant application forms according to the portal instructions. Step 6: Prepare Supporting Documents Compile: CV Motivation letter Transcripts School certificate where applicable Previous university degree where applicable German-language certificate Relevant optional evidence Step 7: Translate Documents Where Necessary Documents not already in German or English should be translated as instructed. The translation should be uploaded together with the original document. Step 8: Upload Everything in PDF Format Upload the application form and supporting documents through the DAAD portal. Step 9: Submit Before October 30 The annual application deadline is: 30 October at 23:59 Central European Time. For the summer 2027 cycle, candidates should therefore submit by: 30 October 2026 at 23:59 CET. Application Opening Date Applications are possible beginning: 1 September each year. For the 2027 summer-course cycle, this means the application window runs from: 1 September 2026 to 30 October 2026. Application Deadline The final deadline is: 30 October 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time Applicants in other time zones should convert the deadline carefully. Do not assume that October 30 means midnight in your own local time. Sustainability Requirement The current DAAD application information also states that applicants commit themselves to: Dealing sensitively with the issue of sustainability. Candidates should therefore pay attention to any sustainability-related information or commitments included in the application and scholarship conditions. How to Write a Strong Motivation Letter 1. Explain Why German Matters to Your Academic Future Make the connection specific. For example, German could help you: Read academic literature Prepare for postgraduate study Work with German research institutions Participate in future exchange programmes Conduct research in Germany Develop technical vocabulary 2. Connect the Course to Your Subject Even though all disciplines are eligible, explain why the chosen course is relevant to your field. An engineering student might emphasize technical German. A historian might emphasize German-language primary sources. A political science student might discuss German or European policy research. 3. Explain Your Future Academic Project DAAD explicitly assesses motivation in relation to the applicant s: Future academic project. A strong application therefore looks beyond the four-week course and explains what the applicant intends to do afterward. 4. Demonstrate Existing Commitment to German Since applicants already need German-language competence, show how you have developed your skills. Possible examples include: University language courses Goethe-Institut study Independent learning Previous certificates German-language academic activities 5. Research Your Course Preferences Do not choose three summer courses randomly. Explain why the overall programme and selected course type support your development. Scholarship Benefits at a Glance Programme: University Summer Courses offered in Germany for Foreign Students and Graduates Provider: German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) Funding source: German Federal Foreign Office Country: Germany Course duration: Four weeks Teaching: At least 25 hours per week Format: In person only Teaching language: German Programme period: June–September 2027 Course fees: Covered Accommodation: Provided in a single room One-time allowance: €475 Travel support: Country-specific allowance for selected countries Health insurance: Included Accident insurance: Included Personal liability insurance: Included Application opening: 1 September 2026 Application deadline: 30 October 2026 at 23:59 CET Application Checklist Before submitting, confirm that you: Are studying at an eligible university outside Germany. Will remain enrolled throughout the scholarship period. Are at least 18 by the start of the summer course. Meet the academic-stage requirement. Have completed at least two university years if applying as an undergraduate. Meet your country-specific German requirement. Have a valid accepted German-language certificate. Have not previously received this programme s funding. Have selected three appropriate course preferences. Have prepared your CV. Have written your motivation letter. Have recent academic transcripts. Have your school-leaving certificate if required. Have your previous university degree if required. Have translated documents where necessary. Have uploaded every required document. Submit before 30 October 2026 at 23:59 CET. Important Note on Country-Specific Requirements The DAAD scholarship database requires applicants to select their: Status Country of application before accessing the relevant application pathway. The programme is explicitly restricted to: Specified countries. Country-specific details may differ, particularly regarding: Minimum German level Accepted documentation Travel allowance Application-document language Applicants should therefore rely on the version of the scholarship listing generated after selecting their own country. Why Consider the DAAD University Summer Courses Scholarship? For students already learning German, this programme offers an unusual combination of: Intensive language study Cultural immersion Academic development Accommodation Financial support International experience Four weeks of intensive teaching at a minimum of 25 hours per week can provide considerably greater language exposure than occasional classes during a normal semester. The opportunity can be particularly useful for students planning future: Master s study in Germany Doctoral research Exchange programmes Academic collaboration Careers involving German institutions International professional work It can also provide an accessible introduction to studying and living in Germany before committing to a longer degree programme. Official Information and Application Applicants should use the official DAAD Scholarship Database for the current country-specific eligibility and application instructions. Official DAAD University Summer Courses Scholarship page The DAAD page provides access to: Course listings Application requirements Application procedure FAQs DAAD portal instructions Country-specific eligibility information Conclusion The DAAD University Summer Courses Scholarship 2027 provides international university students with an opportunity to spend four intensive weeks in Germany strengthening their German-language skills while gaining greater knowledge of German culture and regional studies. The programme is open across academic disciplines and funds German-language, cultural studies and technical-language courses delivered by participating institutions in Germany. Successful scholarship holders receive course-fee coverage, accommodation in a single room, a €475 one-time allowance, health, accident and personal liability insurance, and country-specific travel support for eligible applicants from selected countries . Courses take place between June and September 2027 , last four weeks and provide at least 25 teaching hours per week. All courses are conducted in German and participation is exclusively in person. Applicants must be enrolled at an eligible university outside Germany both when applying and during the scholarship period. Undergraduate students must have completed at least two university years by the beginning of the funded course. Applicants must also demonstrate sufficient German-language ability and submit an accepted language certificate. Selection is competitive and considers both academic achievement and the strength of the applicant s motivation, particularly the connection between German-language study and future academic plans. Applications for the 2027 summer-course cycle are open from 1 September 2026 and must be submitted by: 30 October 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time. For international students who already possess some German and want an intensive, funded opportunity to improve their skills while experiencing academic life in Germany, the DAAD University Summer Courses programme is a particularly valuable short-term study opportunity. title: FASPE Journalism Fellowship 2027: Fully Funded Two-Week Ethics Programme for Journalism Students and Early-Career Journalists in Germany and Poland
summary: Applications are now open for the 2027 FASPE Journalism Fellowship , a fully funded international programme for graduate students with journalism experience and early-career journalists who want to examine professional ethics, ethical leadership, responsibility, media power and the role of journalists in democratic society. The Fellowships at Auschwitz for the Study of Professional Ethics (FASPE) Journalism programme brings a small cohort of approximately 13 to 16 Journalism Fellows to Germany and Poland for an intensive two-week programme combining seminars, historical site visits, interdisciplinary discussion and sustained reflection on the ethical responsibilities of journalists. For the 2027 cycle, the Journalism Fellowship will take place from: June 18, 2027 to July 2, 2027 Applications are open until: January 3, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET Two letters of recommendation are required separately and are due on: January 10, 2027. The Fellowship is fully funded . FASPE covers programme costs and related travel so that a candidate s financial circumstances do not determine whether they can participate. Covered expenses include airfare to and from Europe, programme transportation in Germany and Poland, hotel accommodation, admission costs, programme materials, group meals and pocket money for meals not provided as part of the group programme. FASPE confirms that participants travelling from outside the United States can also have their travel to Berlin and return travel covered. Importantly, applicants do not need to be U.S. citizens or U.S. residents . FASPE accepts eligible applicants regardless of citizenship or residence, although selected Fellows are responsible for arranging any visas they need; FASPE provides supporting documentation for visa applications. About the FASPE Journalism Fellowship FASPE is an intensive professional ethics programme that uses the history of professionals working in Germany and Europe during the Nazi period as a framework for examining ethical responsibility in contemporary professional life. The Journalism Fellowship focuses particularly on the behavior, decisions and responsibilities of journalists. Participants examine how German and international journalists: Reported Nazi policies Failed to report important developments adequately Misrepresented events Normalized dangerous developments Used or failed to use their professional influence Responded to political pressure Navigated institutional and personal responsibility FASPE then uses these historical examples to encourage Fellows to confront the ethical challenges journalists face today. The programme is therefore unusual because it does not treat journalism ethics simply as a collection of professional rules. Instead, Fellows are encouraged to ask more difficult questions about: Personal responsibility Professional identity Institutional pressure Moral judgment Ethical leadership Power Accountability Public trust The consequences of professional decisions FASPE Is Not a Holocaust Studies Programme Prospective applicants should understand what the Fellowship is—and what it is not. FASPE explicitly states that it is: Not a Holocaust studies course Not a genocide-prevention programme The history of the Nazi period is central to the Fellowship, but it functions as an ethical framework through which participants examine their responsibilities in contemporary professional settings. The objective is not simply to learn what happened historically. Rather, Fellows are asked to consider questions such as: What responsibilities does an individual journalist have inside a large institution? When does professional compliance become ethical failure? How can journalists recognize when apparently normal professional practices are contributing to wider harm? How should journalists react when political, financial or institutional pressures influence reporting? What is the relationship between legality and ethical responsibility? When should journalists challenge their own organizations? How should professional influence be exercised responsibly? This makes FASPE particularly relevant to journalism students and early-career journalists interested in the relationship between media institutions and ethical decision-making. 2027 Programme Dates The 2027 Journalism programme runs from: June 18 to July 2, 2027. Journalism Fellows travel during the same programme period as Fellows in: Medicine Clergy and Religious Leadership This shared travel structure allows for interdisciplinary discussion among people preparing for very different professions. FASPE also operates fellowship programmes in: Business Law Design and Technology Medicine Clergy and Religious Leadership Journalism Each programme examines professional ethics through questions specific to that profession while also creating opportunities for Fellows from different fields to engage with one another. Where Does the Fellowship Take Place? The Fellowship is conducted primarily in: Germany and Poland Journalism Fellows spend approximately two weeks travelling through historically significant locations while participating in intensive seminars. The programme uses what FASPE describes as the “power of place” —the idea that ethical questions can be understood differently when discussed in the locations where historical professional decisions had real consequences. Programme activities include: Daily seminars Historical site visits Profession-specific discussions Interdisciplinary sessions Shared meals Informal conversations Group activities The combination of place, history and academic discussion is central to the Fellowship model. How Many Journalism Fellows Are Selected? Each year, FASPE Journalism generally selects: 13 to 16 Fellows from a large applicant pool. The relatively small cohort allows participants to engage in intensive discussion rather than attend a large lecture-style programme. FASPE emphasizes that Fellows should be able to participate constructively in discussions involving difficult, controversial and emotionally demanding subjects. The programme therefore looks not only at academic or professional achievements but also at the applicant s ability to contribute meaningfully to a small intellectual community. What Does the FASPE Journalism Fellowship Cover? FASPE describes its Fellowships as: Fully funded so that financial ability does not affect participation. The programme covers substantial travel and participation expenses. Airfare FASPE covers: Round-trip economy-class airfare for Fellowship travel. Its FAQ specifies airfare from the United States to Europe, while also confirming that Fellows travelling from outside the United States can have their travel to Berlin and return travel covered. This is especially important for international applicants. Transportation in Germany and Poland The Fellowship covers transportation associated with: Group travel Programme activities Travel between programme locations during the Germany and Poland portion of the programme. Participants therefore do not need to finance normal group transportation connected with the Fellowship itinerary. Hotel Accommodation FASPE covers: All hotel costs associated with the programme. Accommodation arrangements are made as part of the Fellowship structure. Meals The programme covers: All group meals and also provides: Pocket money for non-group meals. This makes the financial package considerably more comprehensive than a programme that covers only airfare and accommodation. Admission Fees and Programme Materials FASPE also pays for: Admission fees associated with programme visits Programme materials Participants therefore do not need to pay separately for required historical-site admissions or core academic materials. Who Can Apply for the FASPE Journalism Fellowship? FASPE identifies three main eligibility pathways for Journalism applicants. An applicant should generally fall into one of the following categories. Category 1: Graduate Students With Journalism Experience Applicants may be: Enrolled in a graduate programme of any kind Have some journalism experience Plan to work as a journalist The graduate programme does not necessarily need to be a journalism degree . This means a candidate could potentially be studying another field at graduate level while developing a serious journalism career, provided they already have some journalistic experience and intend to work professionally as a journalist. Journalistic experience may include work in: A university newsroom Student media Professional media Independent journalism Other relevant settings Category 2: Bachelor s Graduates Working as Journalists Applicants can also qualify if they: Have completed an undergraduate degree Are currently working as journalists This pathway is particularly relevant to early-career reporters and other journalism professionals who entered the industry after completing university. Category 3: Graduate-Degree Holders Working as Journalists Applicants may also qualify if they: Have completed a graduate degree Are working as journalists The degree itself does not appear to need to be exclusively in journalism, provided the candidate is professionally working in journalism and otherwise fits the programme s early-career orientation. Early-Career Requirement FASPE seeks Journalism Fellows who are: Preparing for or in the early stages of their careers. Candidates generally should have: No more than 10 years of total professional experience. This is not designed primarily for highly established senior journalists with decades of professional experience. The programme focuses on people who are still developing their: Professional identity Ethical framework Leadership approach Understanding of their role within journalism Published Journalism Is Preferred FASPE states that preference will be given to candidates whose journalism has been: Published, or Aired by a: Recognized news organization. This is described as a preference rather than an absolute eligibility condition. Applicants should therefore not necessarily exclude themselves because they do not have major national publication credits. However, candidates with relevant published work should make it clearly visible in their application. Types of Journalists FASPE Welcomes FASPE seeks Journalism Fellows with diverse professional interests. Potential candidates may be pursuing careers as: Reporters Editors Photojournalists Documentary journalists Nonfiction writers Broadcasters Multimedia journalists Other forms of journalistic storyteller FASPE welcomes journalism conducted in: Local contexts National contexts International contexts The Fellowship is therefore not restricted to newspaper reporters or traditional print journalism. What Qualities Does FASPE Look for? Selection is not based solely on the prestige of an applicant s newsroom or university. FASPE seeks people at a formative stage of their professional lives who demonstrate characteristics such as: Open-mindedness Self-reflection Leadership potential Intellectual maturity Emotional maturity Capacity for respectful disagreement Ability to participate in difficult conversations Potential to influence their profession FASPE evaluates candidates based on their: Academic background Personal experience Professional experience Leadership capacity Potential contribution to the Fellowship Potential contribution to the alumni community No U.S. Citizenship Requirement FASPE is based in the United States, but international applicants are welcome. The programme explicitly states: Applicants do not need to be American or reside in the United States. Eligible candidates may apply: Regardless of citizenship or residency. This makes the Fellowship genuinely international. Applicants may therefore potentially come from countries across: Africa Asia Europe North America Latin America and the Caribbean Middle East Oceania provided they meet the Journalism Fellowship eligibility requirements. Visa Requirements for International Fellows International applicants should understand that FASPE does not arrange visas on behalf of Fellows. Selected participants are responsible for: Making their own visa arrangements. However, FASPE provides the necessary supporting documentation to assist selected Fellows with visa applications. Candidates should therefore ensure that they are able to travel to Germany and Poland during the programme dates if selected. No Religious, Racial or Gender Preference Because FASPE s historical curriculum includes the Holocaust and Nazi Germany, applicants sometimes assume the programme might prioritize candidates of a particular religious background. FASPE explicitly says this is not the case . There are no preferences based on: Religion Race Ideology Political background Gender Socioeconomic status The organization also states that it welcomes applicants of diverse backgrounds and gender identities. Selection is based on eligibility, professional and academic experience, leadership potential and the applicant s capacity to contribute to the Fellowship. What Journalism Ethics Topics Are Discussed? The programme covers several major contemporary ethical challenges. Journalistic Complicity and Misrepresentation Fellows examine how German and international journalists participated in or enabled Nazi policy through: Inadequate coverage Misrepresentation Professional compromise The goal is not merely to assign historical blame. Rather, participants ask what these cases reveal about contemporary journalists responsibilities when institutions or political systems begin to normalize harmful behavior. Technology and Journalism FASPE also examines: The impact of technology on journalism. This topic has become increasingly important as journalists work in an environment shaped by: Social media Artificial intelligence Algorithmic distribution Digital publishing Platform economics Rapid information circulation Participants can consider how technological systems affect both professional practice and ethical responsibility. Journalism and Electoral Politics Another theme concerns the role of journalists in: Electoral politics Democratic accountability Holding power to account Journalists frequently have to balance: Neutrality Scrutiny Public interest Access Fairness Accountability FASPE provides a space for Fellows to examine those tensions through an ethical rather than purely technical lens. Advocacy Journalism Participants examine: The nature and propriety of advocacy journalism. Questions can include: Can a journalist advocate and still be fair? What responsibilities come with taking a public position? Does neutrality always serve the public? When can advocacy undermine journalistic trust? These questions are especially relevant in coverage involving: Human rights Climate change Conflict Social justice Public health Normalizing Aberrant Behavior FASPE also examines how media coverage can: Normalize aberrant behavior through repetition, framing or treatment as ordinary political or social activity. This raises important questions about: Language Headlines Framing False equivalence Newsworthiness Repetition Context Participants are encouraged to consider how routine journalistic practices can sometimes produce unintended ethical consequences. Fake News and Accusations of Fake News The Fellowship also addresses reporting in an environment where: Disinformation is widespread Journalists are regularly accused of producing “fake news” Trust in media institutions may be weak Fellows consider how journalists can maintain: Accuracy Verification Independence Transparency Credibility while operating within polarized information environments. Access Journalism Another ethical question concerns: Access tactics and the trade-offs involved in maintaining access to: Politicians Government officials Institutions Powerful sources Journalists frequently face the possibility that aggressive scrutiny may reduce future access, while excessive accommodation may undermine independence. FASPE encourages Fellows to examine where ethical responsibility lies when professional incentives conflict with public-interest reporting. Interdisciplinary Learning Journalism Fellows do not study entirely separately from other professional cohorts. During the 2027 programme they travel alongside: Medical Fellows Clergy and Religious Leaders Fellows Participants share: Meals Activities Some seminars This structure allows journalists to compare their ethical responsibilities with those of professionals in areas such as: Medicine Religion Institutional leadership FASPE believes this interdisciplinary element helps participants understand professional ethics beyond the assumptions of their own field. The Fellowship Continues Beyond the Two-Week Programme The FASPE experience does not end when participants return home. Fellows become part of a lifetime alumni network that now includes more than 900 alumni across FASPE s professional programmes . FASPE supports continuing engagement through activities such as: Alumni gatherings Online education Writing Lectures Symposia Professional networking Social networking For emerging journalists, this network can create long-term connections with professionals who share an interest in ethical leadership. Where Former Journalism Fellows Work Former FASPE Journalism Fellows have gone on to careers as: Editors Reporters Nonfiction writers Photojournalists Broadcasters Other media professionals FASPE emphasizes that Fellows frequently form long-lasting personal and professional relationships through their shared programme experience. Connection With Columbia Journalism School The FASPE Journalism programme was originally developed in consultation with faculty from: Columbia Journalism School. The programme has since developed its own international alumni network and interdisciplinary professional-ethics model. How to Apply FASPE requires all candidates to use its online application portal. Apply for the 2027 FASPE Journalism Fellowship Applicants should carefully review the application instructions before submitting. Application Requirement 1: Online Form Applicants must complete the online application form. It requests basic information including: Contact details Educational institutions attended Recommendation writers References Candidates should ensure that names and contact details are accurate, particularly because recommendation letters are handled separately through Submittable. Application Requirement 2: Resume or CV Applicants must submit a: Resume or curriculum vitae The document should include: Educational history Employment history Honors Awards Publications where applicable Journalism candidates should make relevant experience particularly easy to identify. This could include: Newsroom positions Freelance work Internships Student journalism Publications Broadcast work Documentary projects Reporting awards Application Requirement 3: Academic Transcripts Applicants must provide transcripts from institutions of higher education where they spent significant periods of study. FASPE accepts: Electronic transcripts Scanned hard-copy transcripts Unofficial transcripts However: Screenshots of online transcripts are not accepted. Applicants do not normally need to submit transcripts for brief experiences such as: A single semester abroad One summer course What If You Are a First-Year Graduate Student? Applicants in the first year of a programme may not yet have grades available. In that situation, FASPE allows the applicant to provide a letter from the relevant dean confirming: Enrollment in the degree programme Good academic standing Ideally, current courses A general admissions letter or registrar letter that does not identify the degree programme is not sufficient. Application Requirement 4: Journalism Short Essays Journalism candidates must respond to: Programme-specific short essay questions. These questions are intended to give FASPE insight into the applicant s: Motivation Professional identity Ethical thinking Capacity for reflection Leadership potential Ability to engage with difficult questions The current How to Apply page provides the Journalism short-essay materials for the 2027 cycle. Applicants should take these essays seriously. The Fellowship is built around discussion and self-examination, so reflective writing may be just as important as demonstrating professional accomplishments. Application Requirement 5: Two Letters of Recommendation Applicants need: Two recommendation letters from: Academic faculty, or Professional references For students, FASPE generally prefers recommendations from academic faculty who have taught the candidate in their current or most recent graduate programme. However, recommendations can also come from: Previous graduate faculty Undergraduate professors Professional supervisors Employers particularly for early-career professionals. Recommendation Letter Deadline An important detail is that recommendation letters have a later deadline than the main application. Applicant deadline: January 3, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET Recommendation deadline: January 10, 2027 Letters must be submitted: Directly by the recommenders through Submittable. Applicants should therefore enter referee information early enough to give recommenders adequate preparation time. What FASPE Wants Recommenders to Address FASPE says recommendation letters can usefully discuss areas including: Academic work Relevant professional experience Experiences that would enrich discussions about professional ethics Participation in discussion Written and verbal communication Responses to intellectually or emotionally intense situations Ability to work and travel in small groups Leadership potential Professional strengths and weaknesses Candidates should therefore select recommenders who know them meaningfully rather than choosing only the most prestigious person available. How FASPE Selects Fellows FASPE evaluates candidates using a combination of: Academic background Professional experience Personal experience Leadership potential Capacity for self-reflection Potential contribution to discussions Potential contribution to the alumni network The Fellowship is especially interested in applicants who are willing to question their own assumptions and participate respectfully in challenging conversations. Preparing a Competitive FASPE Journalism Application 1. Demonstrate Real Journalism Commitment If you are still studying, explain why journalism is not simply an extracurricular interest. Show evidence such as: Reporting Student media Freelance publication Newsroom experience Documentary work Broadcast work and explain where you want your journalism career to go. 2. Do Not Treat the Ethics Essays Like Generic Personal Statements FASPE is specifically about professional ethics. The strongest responses are likely to engage seriously with: Ambiguity Responsibility Professional pressure Personal vulnerability Institutional power Avoid writing only that ethics is “important.” Explain how ethical conflicts actually arise in journalism. 3. Be Willing to Examine Your Own Vulnerabilities A programme centered on ethical leadership is likely to value applicants who can identify the circumstances under which they themselves might make poor professional decisions. For example: Pressure to publish quickly Desire for access Career ambition Organizational loyalty Political assumptions Fear of professional consequences Self-reflection is stronger than presenting yourself as someone who would never make an ethical mistake. 4. Highlight Published Work Clearly Because FASPE gives preference to applicants whose journalism has been published or broadcast by recognized news organizations, include relevant work prominently. Provide clear information about: Outlet Date Role Type of journalism where appropriate. 5. Choose Recommenders Who Can Discuss How You Think A useful FASPE recommendation is not merely: “This candidate received excellent grades.” A stronger referee can discuss: How you respond to disagreement How you think through difficult problems Your judgment Your leadership potential How you operate in groups 6. Show That You Can Participate in Difficult Dialogue FASPE explicitly seeks Fellows capable of discussing controversial and emotionally difficult issues: Responsibly and respectfully. Your application should show intellectual confidence without presenting yourself as unwilling to reconsider your assumptions. Key Details at a Glance Programme: FASPE Journalism Fellowship Year: 2027 Programme dates: June 18–July 2, 2027 Locations: Germany and Poland Duration: Approximately two weeks Number of Journalism Fellows: Around 13–16 Primary focus: Professional ethics and ethical leadership in journalism Target applicants: Graduate students with journalism experience and early-career journalists Career stage: Generally no more than 10 years of professional experience Funding: Fully funded Airfare: Covered Programme transportation: Covered Hotels: Covered Admission fees: Covered Programme materials: Covered Group meals: Covered Pocket money for non-group meals: Provided Citizenship restriction: None Application platform: Submittable Main application deadline: January 3, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET Recommendation deadline: January 10, 2027 Official FASPE Journalism Fellowship information FASPE 2027 application instructions Conclusion The FASPE Journalism Fellowship 2027 offers journalism students and early-career journalists an unusual opportunity to spend two intensive weeks in Germany and Poland examining some of the most difficult ethical questions confronting the profession. Rather than functioning as a conventional journalism skills course, the Fellowship focuses on the deeper responsibilities associated with being a journalist. Participants examine the conduct of journalists during the Nazi period and use those historical cases to explore contemporary questions involving media power, political accountability, technology, advocacy journalism, misinformation, professional access and the normalization of harmful behavior. Approximately 13 to 16 Journalism Fellows are selected each year. Eligible applicants generally include graduate students with journalism experience who plan to enter the profession, Bachelor s graduates currently working as journalists, and graduate-degree holders working as journalists. FASPE generally seeks candidates with no more than ten years of professional experience. The Fellowship is particularly accessible because it is fully funded . FASPE covers airfare, programme transportation, hotels, admission costs, materials, group meals and pocket money for meals outside organized group activities. International applicants are also eligible for travel support. There is no U.S. citizenship or residency requirement , and FASPE explicitly welcomes eligible applicants regardless of nationality. It also states that there are no preferences based on race, religion, ideology, political background, gender or socioeconomic status. The 2027 Journalism programme will run from June 18 to July 2, 2027 . Applications must be submitted through Submittable by: January 3, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET and the two required recommendation letters must arrive by: January 10, 2027. For emerging journalists interested not simply in how to report, but in what responsibilities come with the power to report, the FASPE Journalism Fellowship offers a distinctive opportunity for professional reflection, international learning and long-term engagement with an interdisciplinary community of ethical leaders.
