title: James Kane Foundation Grants 2026: Up to £400,000 Annual Funding for Education, STEM and Employment Pathways in Northern Ireland
summary: The James Kane Foundation has opened its 2026 Expression of Interest process for organisations seeking funding for projects that improve access to education, STEM opportunities, career development, work experience, training and pathways into employment across Northern Ireland . Established in 2016 through the legacy of the late James “Jim” Walker Kane , owner of JW Kane Precision Engineering Limited, the Foundation supports initiatives designed to help people develop the education, skills, competencies and career opportunities needed to progress into employment, further study or professional life. For the 2026 funding round, the Foundation expects to allocate approximately: £400,000 per year across its grantmaking programme. Funding may include both: Large grants Small grants below £25,000 The Foundation indicates that approximately: 75% of its annual budget will be allocated to large grants 25% will be allocated to small grants of under £25,000 Multi-year funding may also be considered. The current application process begins with a mandatory Expression of Interest , commonly referred to as an EOI. Organisations whose EOIs are assessed positively may then be invited to submit a full application during Stage 2. The deadline for the 2026 Expression of Interest round is: Friday, 16 October 2026 at 12:00 noon Applicants should note carefully that the closing time is midday , not midnight. Projects funded through this round will normally be expected to commence from: June 2027 The Foundation particularly welcomes projects aligned with two priority themes: Enabling STEM-related education and career opportunities Helping students make informed choices between employment, career and higher-level education pathways Applications are open to eligible organisations including: Schools Colleges Third-level institutions Employers Private-sector companies Charities Social enterprises Priority may be given to projects benefiting people living in the Armagh, Banbridge and Craigavon Council areas , although the Foundation’s broader area of benefit extends across Northern Ireland. About the James Kane Foundation The James Kane Foundation was established in 2016 . Its funding comes from the legacy of the late James Walker Kane , also known as Jim Kane, who owned JW Kane Precision Engineering Limited. The Foundation was created with a strong connection to: Education Skills Employment Engineering Career development Training Economic opportunity Its charitable objects focus on advancing education for public benefit, particularly in Portadown and surrounding areas , while also allowing support for projects elsewhere in Northern Ireland. The Foundation may support people and organisations through activities connected with: Work experience Employment opportunities Training Career preparation Skills development Professional development Preparation for entry into occupations, trades or professions However, the Foundation does not intend to replace funding for services that schools, colleges, government bodies or other public authorities already have a legal obligation to provide. Who Governs the James Kane Foundation? The Foundation is governed by a: Board of Trustees with experience across: Business Education The Trustees collectively make decisions concerning: Grant awards Funding priorities Project support Strategic direction The Foundation is administered by: Belfast Charitable Society which supports the Trustees in delivering the Foundation’s aims and charitable objectives. This governance structure means applicants should prepare proposals that are not only socially valuable but also: Clearly structured Financially credible Educationally relevant Deliverable Capable of demonstrating measurable outcomes Purpose of the 2026 Funding Round The Foundation’s core mission is to: Progress and facilitate education and career opportunities. Projects seeking support must clearly demonstrate how they contribute to this mission. Applications that fall outside education, career development, STEM access or transitions into employment are unlikely to be competitive. The Foundation has identified two principal themes for eligible projects. Theme 1: Enabling STEM-Related Education and Career Opportunities The first funding theme focuses on improving access to opportunities connected with: Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics or: STEM Projects under this theme may seek to help participants: Discover STEM careers Develop technical skills Gain practical experience Engage with employers Access engineering opportunities Understand pathways into STEM education Build confidence in science and technology Prepare for technical employment Access skills training Participate in work experience The Foundation’s origins in the legacy of a precision engineering business make STEM and employment development particularly relevant to its charitable objectives. What Could a STEM Project Look Like? The Foundation does not provide an exhaustive list of eligible activities, but qualifying projects might potentially include initiatives such as: Engineering outreach STEM career programmes Employer engagement Robotics programmes Coding opportunities Technology workshops Practical engineering experience STEM mentoring Career fairs Skills development programmes STEM-related work placements Technical training The important consideration is not simply whether a project uses the label “STEM.” Applicants need to show how their activity creates additional and meaningful education or career opportunities. Theme 2: Helping Students Make Informed Education and Career Choices The second priority theme concerns helping students make informed decisions between: Employment Career pathways Higher-level education Many young people face uncertainty when deciding what to do after: School College Training Further education The Foundation is interested in projects that help students better understand the options available to them. This could include initiatives helping participants understand: University pathways Apprenticeships Vocational training Employment opportunities Professional careers Technical careers Further education Skills requirements Why Career Decision-Making Matters Students may have limited information about: Different industries Entry requirements Apprenticeships Career progression Workplace expectations Alternative pathways to university Good career guidance can help individuals make choices aligned with their: Skills Interests Strengths Ambitions Financial circumstances Projects under this theme should therefore demonstrate how they improve the quality of information, experience or support available to learners. Additionality Is a Key Requirement The James Kane Foundation specifically states that it seeks: Additionality in the projects it funds. This means funding should create something additional to what is already available. Applicants should demonstrate clearly: What currently exists What gap remains What the proposed project adds Why Foundation funding is necessary A project that simply continues standard activity without adding something new may be less competitive. What Additionality Could Mean Additionality may involve: Reaching a new group of participants Expanding access to an existing opportunity Introducing an innovative programme Creating a new employer partnership Developing a new training pathway Providing an opportunity not previously available Testing a new model Bringing STEM resources to underserved communities Applicants should explain additionality directly rather than expecting Trustees to infer it. Projects the Foundation Will Not Fund The Foundation states that it will not support activities that Trustees believe are the responsibility of: Local authorities Government Public bodies with statutory obligations This means funding cannot simply substitute for services that should already be delivered through public funding. The Foundation will also avoid funding projects that: Duplicate existing provision. Applicants therefore need to research existing services and demonstrate that their project fills a genuine gap. Avoiding Duplication A strong application should explain: What similar services currently exist How the proposed activity differs Which participants are currently underserved Why another service is necessary Whether the project complements rather than duplicates other organisations This is particularly important in areas where several organisations are already delivering similar education or employment programmes. Geographic Priority: Armagh, Banbridge and Craigavon The Foundation may give particular priority to projects benefiting people in the: Armagh, Banbridge and Craigavon Council areas. This geographic priority reflects the Foundation’s historical connection to: Portadown Surrounding communities However, the Foundation’s objects allow activity elsewhere in: Northern Ireland Projects outside the priority council area may therefore still be eligible where they fit the wider mission and criteria. Approximately £400,000 Available Annually The James Kane Foundation intends to allocate approximately: £400,000 per year through its grantmaking. This does not mean a single organisation can apply for £400,000. Rather, this is the approximate total annual funding envelope available across funded projects. Applicants should request only what is justified by: Project scope Delivery plan Outputs Outcomes Budget Large and Small Grants The Foundation plans to divide its annual budget broadly as follows: Large Grants Approximately: 75% of the annual budget will be allocated to larger grants. The information provided does not specify a single maximum amount for a large grant. Applicants considering a substantial request should therefore review the detailed guidance carefully rather than assuming a particular upper limit. Small Grants Approximately: 25% of the budget will be allocated to: Small grants below £25,000 This makes the programme potentially suitable for both: Smaller pilot projects Larger strategic initiatives Multi-Year Funding Is Possible The Foundation states that it will consider: Multi-year funding This can be valuable for projects requiring more than one year to: Develop Recruit participants Deliver training Measure outcomes Establish partnerships However, multi-year funding should not be assumed automatically. Applicants should provide a clear case for why several years of funding are necessary. When Can Projects Begin? Projects supported through the current round will normally be funded only if they commence from: June 2027 Applicants should therefore plan: Recruitment Staffing Procurement Partnerships Programme delivery around the expected funding commencement date. Projects requiring funding significantly before June 2027 may not align with the Foundation’s normal timetable. Match Funding Is Allowed The James Kane Foundation allows its grants to be combined with: Match funding Other secured funding sources This means applicants do not necessarily need the Foundation to finance the entire project. Indeed, applications that can demonstrate: Secured match funding may be viewed more favourably. Why Match Funding Can Strengthen an Application Match funding can demonstrate: Wider confidence in the project Shared commitment Financial sustainability Partnership Lower dependence on one funder Stronger leverage of Foundation resources Applicants should clearly state: How much match funding has been secured Who is providing it What costs it will cover Whether it is confirmed or pending Do not describe unconfirmed funding as secured. Partnership Funding Is Encouraged The Foundation states that it is willing to work with: Other organisations Other funders where collaboration can: Maximise impact Increase resources Improve project delivery This may be particularly useful for larger education or STEM initiatives involving: Schools Universities Employers Charities Industry bodies Community organisations Eligible Project Costs The Foundation may support several types of direct project costs. These can include: Project Costs Funding may support costs directly required to deliver the proposed programme. Salary Costs The Foundation may support salary costs where they are clearly connected to the project. This could include staff required specifically for: Project coordination Training Delivery Participant support Equipment Costs Equipment may also be eligible where it is clearly required for project delivery. For STEM programmes, this could be particularly relevant where projects need technical equipment. Funding Requests Must Be Clearly Connected to Outcomes Every cost should be linked to: Project activities Outputs Outcomes Applicants should avoid submitting broad or poorly justified budgets. For example, instead of requesting a generic equipment budget, explain: What equipment is required Who will use it Why it is necessary What educational outcome it enables Overhead and Indirect Costs Are Normally Not Funded The Foundation generally does not seek to fund: General overheads Indirect organisational costs because its priority is supporting: New and/or innovative projects that directly align with its mission. Applicants should therefore avoid including large general administrative charges unless there is a compelling project-specific justification. Organisational Reserves May Be Reviewed The Foundation may request further information concerning: Organisational reserves Applicants should therefore be prepared to explain: Current reserves Financial position Why Foundation support is necessary This helps Trustees understand whether the requested funding represents appropriate use of philanthropic resources. Who Can Apply? The James Kane Foundation accepts applications from several categories of organisations. Eligible applicants include: Education Bodies Such as: Schools Colleges Third-level institutions Employers Including: Private-sector companies Charities Eligible charitable organisations may apply where the project aligns with the mission and themes. Social Enterprises Social enterprises can also apply if they meet the programme requirements. Can Individuals Apply? The information provided describes eligible applicants as organisations rather than individuals. It does not list: Individual students Individual researchers Individual jobseekers as direct applicants. The funding is therefore primarily designed to support organisations delivering projects for beneficiaries. Individuals may benefit from funded projects but are not identified as direct applicants under the published eligibility categories. One Application Per Organisation The Foundation will consider: Only one application per organisation in each grant round. This is an important restriction. Organisations with multiple possible projects should decide internally which application represents their strongest fit with the Foundation’s priorities. Submitting several applications from different departments of the same organisation may not be accepted. Can an Organisation Receive Funding More Than Once? Yes. The Foundation may fund the same organisation more than once over time. However: It will not provide multiple awards to the same organisation within the same funding cycle. Future applications from previous grantees are considered on a: Case-by-case basis and are usually dependent on satisfactory performance against previous: Outputs Outcomes Organisations that have previously received funding should therefore be prepared to demonstrate the impact of earlier awards. The Application Process The James Kane Foundation uses a: Two-stage application process consisting of: Expression of Interest Full Application The purpose of the two-stage structure is to allow the Foundation to assess project fit before asking applicants to prepare a more detailed full submission. Stage 1: Expression of Interest The first stage is the: Expression of Interest or: EOI This allows applicants to present: Their project concept Relevant organisational information Supporting evidence The EOI is therefore an important screening stage. Applicants should not treat it as an informal preliminary note. Expression of Interest Form Requirements The Foundation has strict formatting instructions. Applications must be completed using the official forms provided. They must be submitted in: Microsoft Word format Applicants must: Leave the form formatting unchanged Not add photographs Not add images Not insert extra text boxes Applications submitted: In another format With altered formatting will not be accepted. Word Limits Must Be Followed Many questions in the EOI form include: Maximum word counts Applicants must not exceed these limits. Information provided beyond the stated limit may: Be treated as ineligible Not be considered This means applicants should write strategically. Prioritize: Need Project design Outcomes Fit Evidence rather than lengthy background information. No Unrequested Additional Documents Applicants cannot attach additional supporting papers unless the Foundation specifically requests them. Do not attempt to strengthen an application by sending: Extra brochures Large reports Promotional materials Unrequested case studies The application should stand on the evidence permitted within the formal process. Required Supporting Documents The EOI form sets out the supporting documentation required at Stage 1. Applicants must submit: All requested information for the EOI to be accepted. Incomplete submissions will: Not be assessed and will be rejected. Applicants should therefore use a checklist before sending their application. Data Sharing and Due Diligence The Foundation notes that information supplied through the application process may be shared with: Other funders Government departments Agencies for purposes such as: Audit Research Statutory obligations Crime prevention Crime detection Applicants should therefore ensure all information submitted is: Accurate Complete Verifiable Stage 2: Full Application EOIs undergo assessment after the October deadline. Applications will either: Be rejected, or Proceed to Stage 2 Only successful Stage 1 applicants will move to: The Full Application stage This means applicants should not prepare a complete second-stage application unless invited. When Will EOI Applicants Hear Back? The Foundation expects applicants to be notified approximately: 8–10 weeks after the Expression of Interest deadline Given the deadline of October 16, applicants should therefore expect initial decisions later in 2026. No Appeal Process The James Kane Foundation’s funding decisions are: Final There is: No right of appeal Applicants should therefore ensure their EOI is as complete and persuasive as possible at the time of submission. No Feedback Will Be Provided The Foundation states that: Feedback will not be provided to unsuccessful applicants. Because of this, organisations should carefully self-assess against the eligibility criteria before applying. Expression of Interest Deadline The deadline is: Friday, 16 October 2026 at 12:00 noon Applicants should not assume that the form can be submitted at the end of the business day. The deadline is specifically: 12 PM rather than 5 PM or midnight. Submitting at least a day early is advisable. Download the 2026 EOI Guidance Applicants are strongly encouraged to read the full guidance before preparing their submission. 2026 EOI Guidance The guidance should be reviewed carefully for: Eligibility Funding priorities Application questions Supporting documents Assessment requirements Download the Expression of Interest Form The official 2026 EOI form Applicants must use this form and preserve its original formatting. Key Dates at a Glance EOI forms available: 2026 EOI deadline: Friday, 16 October 2026 at 12:00 noon EOI decision: Approximately 8–10 weeks after the deadline Stage 2: By invitation Normal project funding commencement: June 2027 Funding at a Glance Foundation: James Kane Foundation Approximate annual grant budget: £400,000 Large grants: Approximately 75% of the annual funding budget Small grants: Approximately 25% of the annual budget Small grant threshold: Under £25,000 Multi-year funding: May be considered Match funding: Permitted and potentially advantageous Eligible project costs: Project costs, salary costs and equipment costs where clearly related to the project General overheads: Normally not funded How to Prepare a Strong James Kane Foundation EOI 1. Start With the Foundation’s Mission Your application should clearly demonstrate how the project will: Progress and facilitate education and career opportunities. Do not make the connection vague. State directly what educational or employment outcome the project will create. 2. Align Clearly With One or Both Themes Identify whether the project fits: STEM education and careers Education/employment decision-making or both. Do not submit a general youth programme and assume the Foundation will identify the connection. 3. Demonstrate Additionality Explain: What currently exists What is missing What your programme adds Why it cannot be delivered through existing provision This is one of the Foundation’s explicit priorities. 4. Avoid Statutory Activity Do not apply for services that schools, government or local authorities are already required to provide. The Foundation wants philanthropic funding to create: Additional opportunities rather than replace statutory provision. 5. Demonstrate Need Use evidence to show: Who needs the project What barrier exists How many people are affected Why the issue matters Evidence can make the difference between a general idea and a credible project proposal. 6. Define Outputs Outputs describe what the project will deliver. For example: Number of workshops Number of participants Number of placements Number of mentoring relationships Number of employer sessions These should be realistic and measurable. 7. Define Outcomes Outcomes describe the change created. Examples might include: Improved STEM confidence Increased career awareness Improved technical skills More students entering apprenticeships Better understanding of higher education pathways Increased employment readiness Trustees will want to understand what changes because of the grant. 8. Explain Why Your Organisation Is Well Placed to Deliver Applicants should demonstrate organisational capacity. This may include: Relevant experience Staff expertise Partnerships Existing relationships with schools Employer networks Previous programme outcomes 9. Use Match Funding Strategically If match funding has already been secured, state it clearly. The Foundation says confirmed match funding may be viewed more favourably. Explain: Funding source Amount Confirmation status How it complements the Foundation request 10. Follow the Form Instructions Exactly Technical compliance matters. Do not: Alter the form Add photographs Add text boxes Exceed word limits Submit unrequested documents Even a strong project can be rejected if the application does not comply with formal requirements. Important Details at a Glance Organisation: James Kane Foundation Funding round: 2026 Primary location: Northern Ireland Priority geography: Armagh, Banbridge and Craigavon Funding focus: Education and career opportunities Theme 1: STEM-related education and career opportunities Theme 2: Supporting informed decisions between employment/career and higher-level education Eligible applicants: Education bodies, employers, charities and social enterprises Approximate annual funding: £400,000 Small grants: Under £25,000 Multi-year funding: Possible Application process: Two stages Stage 1: Expression of Interest Stage 2: Full application by invitation EOI deadline: 16 October 2026 at 12:00 noon Normal funded project start: June 2027 EOI Form: https://jameskanefoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/JKF-Expression-of-Interest-2026.docx Guidance: https://jameskanefoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/JKF-EOI-Guidelines-2026.pdf Main information: https://lnkd.in/eWWsuMfC Conclusion The James Kane Foundation 2026 grant round offers an important funding opportunity for eligible organisations delivering education, STEM and career-development projects across Northern Ireland. The Foundation expects to allocate approximately £400,000 per year , with around 75% directed toward larger grants and 25% toward grants below £25,000 . Multi-year funding may also be considered. Applications should support the Foundation’s mission of progressing and facilitating education and career opportunities and must align with at least one of two priority themes: Enabling STEM-related education and career opportunities. Helping students make informed choices between employment/career pathways and higher-level education. Eligible applicants include schools, colleges, third-level institutions, employers, private-sector companies, charities and social enterprises. The Foundation places strong emphasis on additionality , meaning funded programmes should create opportunities beyond what is already available. It will not fund activities that public bodies have a statutory responsibility to deliver or projects that unnecessarily duplicate existing services. Priority may be given to projects benefiting people in Armagh, Banbridge and Craigavon , although the Foundation’s remit extends more broadly across Northern Ireland. Funding may cover project, salary and equipment costs where clearly connected to project outputs and outcomes. General overheads are normally not funded. Match funding is allowed, and applications demonstrating confirmed match funding may receive more favourable consideration. The application process has two stages. Organisations must first submit an Expression of Interest. Successful applicants will then be invited to complete a full application. EOIs must be submitted using the Foundation’s official Word document without modifying its formatting, adding images or exceeding stated word limits. The deadline for Stage 1 is: Friday, 16 October 2026 at 12:00 noon. Applicants are expected to receive an EOI decision approximately 8–10 weeks after the deadline . title: Call for Proposals 2026: Build Your AgriCanvas and Turn Your Cashew Business Idea into a Climate-Smart Venture
summary: Young and emerging entrepreneurs with innovative ideas for the cashew sector now have an opportunity to transform their concepts into investment-ready and climate-smart businesses through the e-MOVE Call for Proposals: Build Your AgriCanvas. Build Your Future. The initiative is designed to support promising agripreneurs who are developing innovative solutions across the cashew value chain. Through a combination of free online learning, business development tools and potential kickstart prizes, participants can strengthen their entrepreneurial ideas and position themselves for future investment and growth. Submission Window 3 is open from September to October 2026 , giving eligible entrepreneurs the opportunity to develop and submit a viable business concept using the AgriCanvas framework. Successful participants may receive valuable support, including EUR 2,000 in direct funding or business-enabling tools such as a laptop, tablet or software to support their operations. The application deadline is 30 October 2026 . What Is the e-MOVE Call for Proposals? The e-MOVE initiative encourages young and emerging entrepreneurs in the agricultural sector to convert knowledge gained through online learning into practical, investment-ready business ideas. Participants are expected to build on the knowledge and tools acquired through free e-learning courses offered on the e-MOVE platform. The programme focuses on helping entrepreneurs understand important areas of modern agribusiness, including sustainable agricultural practices, investment readiness, business planning and climate resilience. The Call for Proposals specifically invites innovative ideas connected to the cashew value chain . Rather than simply submitting a general business idea, applicants are required to demonstrate how their proposed venture can operate as a viable enterprise. This includes developing a clear business model, identifying potential revenue streams, considering climate-smart practices and estimating the capital required to establish or expand the business. The initiative aims to help promising entrepreneurs move from ideas to actionable business concepts that can potentially attract investment and contribute to sustainable agricultural development. Why the Cashew Value Chain Matters Cashew is an important agricultural commodity with significant economic potential across many countries, particularly in Africa and other OACPS member states. However, the potential of the cashew sector extends beyond primary production. The wider value chain offers opportunities in areas such as: Cashew farming and production Sustainable agricultural practices Processing and value addition Cashew nut processing Packaging Storage and logistics Marketing and distribution Agricultural technology Climate-smart production systems Waste management and by-product utilization Agribusiness services Financial and investment solutions Digital platforms supporting farmers and businesses Through this Call for Proposals, entrepreneurs are encouraged to think creatively about challenges and opportunities within the cashew ecosystem. Applicants can develop ideas that improve productivity, increase value addition, strengthen resilience, create employment or introduce innovative business solutions within the sector. What Are the Benefits of the e-MOVE Call for Proposals? The programme provides more than just an opportunity to compete for financial support. Participants also gain access to learning resources and business development tools designed to strengthen their entrepreneurial capacity. 1. Opportunity to Receive EUR 2,000 in Direct Funding Selected winners may receive EUR 2,000 in direct funding to support the development or growth of their business. The funding can provide an important starting point for entrepreneurs seeking to test, launch, strengthen or scale a promising agribusiness concept. For early-stage entrepreneurs, access to initial capital can be a major challenge. This opportunity provides selected participants with the possibility of receiving financial support to move their business idea closer to implementation. 2. Opportunity to Receive Business Equipment or Software Winners may alternatively receive valuable tools to support their business operations, including: A laptop A tablet Software Digital tools are increasingly important for modern businesses. Equipment and software can help entrepreneurs manage operations, maintain records, communicate with customers, develop marketing strategies and improve overall business efficiency. 3. Free Access to Cashew Sector Learning Applicants gain access to free e-learning courses designed to strengthen their understanding of agriculture and agribusiness. The learning pathway helps participants build the knowledge necessary to develop stronger and more practical business ideas. The courses are offered at no cost, meaning participants do not need to pay tuition or registration fees to access the required learning materials. 4. Development of an Investment-Ready Business Idea One of the most important aspects of the programme is its focus on investment readiness. Many entrepreneurs have innovative ideas but struggle to communicate them clearly to investors, partners or financial institutions. The AgriCanvas process helps applicants structure their ideas by considering key elements of a viable business model. Participants are encouraged to think about areas such as: The problem their business intends to solve Their target market The products or services they will offer Revenue generation Required resources Climate resilience Business operations Capital requirements Growth potential This approach can help transform a general business concept into a more structured and fundable proposal. 5. Focus on Climate-Smart and Resilient Agriculture The initiative places significant emphasis on climate-smart and low-emission agricultural practices. Applicants are expected to consider how their projects can contribute to environmental sustainability and resilience. For example, an entrepreneur may consider: Sustainable farming practices Resource-efficient production Climate adaptation strategies Reduced emissions Improved soil conservation Reduced agricultural waste Renewable energy solutions Circular economy approaches Resilient agricultural supply chains By integrating climate-smart approaches into their business models, entrepreneurs can develop ventures that are better positioned to respond to environmental challenges. 6. Opportunity to Contribute to Sustainable Food Systems The programme aims to support agricultural enterprises that can contribute to stronger and more sustainable food systems. Innovative agribusinesses have the potential to: Create employment opportunities Support farmers Increase agricultural productivity Strengthen local economies Improve value addition Reduce post-harvest losses Promote sustainable production Support rural development By supporting viable MSMEs, the initiative seeks to strengthen the role of young entrepreneurs in building resilient agricultural economies. Who Can Apply for the e-MOVE Call for Proposals? The Call for Proposals is designed for young and emerging entrepreneurs with innovative ideas related to the cashew sector. To qualify, applicants must meet the following requirements. Applicants Must Be 18 Years or Older Participants must be at least 18 years old at the time of application. Applicants Must Be Based in an OACPS Member State The opportunity is open to individuals based in member states of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS). The OACPS represents countries across Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific. Applicants should confirm whether their country is an eligible OACPS member state before beginning their application. Applicants Must Have an Innovative Cashew Value Chain Idea The proposed business concept must focus on one or more aspects of the cashew value chain. Applicants are encouraged to identify opportunities where innovation can improve existing systems, address challenges or create new economic opportunities. Applicants Must Complete the Required e-MOVE Training Completion of the mandatory e-learning pathway is an essential requirement. Applicants cannot simply submit an idea without completing the required courses. A valid certificate ID from the final required course must be included in the submission. How to Apply for the e-MOVE Call for Proposals 2026 Applicants must follow a specific process to ensure that their submission is considered valid. The application process involves registration, completion of mandatory courses, development of an AgriCanvas and submission of the final business idea. Step 1: Register on atingi or Access the e-MOVE Landing Page The first step is to access the e-MOVE learning platform through atingi. Applicants can access the dedicated e-MOVE landing page, where the required learning resources are grouped together. The platform provides free courses designed to help participants develop the knowledge necessary to create a stronger agribusiness proposal. Applicants should ensure they create or use an account that allows them to complete the full learning pathway and access their course certificates. Step 2: Complete the Mandatory e-MOVE Courses Applicants must complete the required courses in the specified order. The learning pathway includes two important stages. Course 1: Introduction to Conservation Agriculture The first requirement is to complete the course: Introduction to Conservation Agriculture (CA) This course introduces participants to concepts related to sustainable and conservation-focused agricultural practices. Completing this first stage is necessary before progressing to the next required course. Course 2: Creating an Investment-Ready Agribusiness After successfully completing the first course, participants unlock the next required course: Creating an Investment-Ready Agribusiness This course is particularly important because it prepares applicants to structure their business ideas and develop proposals that demonstrate investment potential. Applicants must complete this course successfully and obtain a valid certificate ID. The certificate ID serves as proof that the applicant has completed the required training pathway. Step 3: Develop Your AgriCanvas After completing the required learning, participants must develop their business concept using the Business Model Canvas template provided in the submission module of the Creating an Investment-Ready Agribusiness course. The AgriCanvas should clearly explain the proposed business idea. Applicants should use this stage to carefully consider the major components of their proposed venture. A strong AgriCanvas should demonstrate: A clear business concept A relevant problem or opportunity The proposed solution Target customers or beneficiaries Revenue generation potential Key business activities Required resources Partnerships Operational considerations Financial requirements Climate-smart features Potential for sustainability and growth Applicants should avoid rushing this stage. A well-developed business model can significantly improve the clarity and strength of a proposal. Step 4: Submit Your Business Idea Through the Official Form Once the AgriCanvas is complete, applicants must submit their proposal through the official submission form. To ensure that a submission is valid, applicants must: Use the certificate ID from the Creating an Investment-Ready Agribusiness course Complete the official submission form Enter the complete AgriCanvas directly into the form Provide all required information Submit through the designated application platform Applicants should note that file uploads for the AgriCanvas are not accepted . The full AgriCanvas must be entered directly into the official form. Only submissions completed through the designated form will be reviewed. Additional Information Required in the Submission Form In addition to the AgriCanvas, applicants will be asked to provide short written information about important aspects of their project. These additional questions are designed to help evaluators understand the practicality and sustainability of the proposed business idea. Describe the Climate-Smart or Resilience Component Applicants must explain how their proposed business contributes to climate resilience or climate-smart agriculture. This could involve demonstrating how the project responds to environmental challenges or promotes more sustainable agricultural practices. Applicants should clearly explain the connection between their business model and climate resilience. Explain the Revenue Model Entrepreneurs must explain how their business intends to generate income. A strong revenue model should clearly demonstrate how the venture can become financially sustainable. Applicants may need to consider questions such as: Who will pay for the product or service? What will customers purchase? How will the business generate revenue? How frequently will revenue be generated? What are the main sources of income? What makes the business financially viable? A clear revenue model is important because it demonstrates that the project is not simply an idea but has the potential to operate as a sustainable enterprise. Estimate the Capital Required Applicants must provide an estimate of the financial resources needed to start or scale the proposed project. This should include a realistic assessment of the capital required for implementation. Potential costs may include: Equipment Raw materials Technology Production Marketing Transportation Staffing Facilities Licensing Business development Applicants should make reasonable and well-considered estimates based on the nature and scale of their proposed venture. Can Applicants Save Their Submission and Return Later? Yes. The KoboToolbox submission form allows applicants to save a draft and return later . This feature gives entrepreneurs the opportunity to take their time when developing their responses. Applicants should use this flexibility to carefully review their AgriCanvas, climate-smart strategy, revenue model and capital requirements before submitting the final application. However, saving a draft should not be confused with submitting the application. Applicants must ensure that the final submission is completed before the deadline. Can You Submit More Than One Business Idea? No. Each applicant may submit only one idea per submission window . Applicants should therefore carefully select the strongest and most viable business concept before completing their application. The organisers have also indicated that where multiple submissions are made using the same course certificate ID, only the last complete and valid submission will be considered. Any additional submissions using the same certificate ID may be disregarded. This makes it particularly important for applicants to review their proposal carefully before submitting it. What Happens If You Are Not Selected? Applicants who are not selected during the current submission window are encouraged not to give up. Entrepreneurship often involves refining and improving ideas over time. Unsuccessful applicants may have the opportunity to: Improve their business concept Strengthen their AgriCanvas Continue learning through e-MOVE Improve their financial projections Develop a stronger climate-smart component Refine their revenue model Resubmit their idea in a future submission window The organisers indicate that unsuccessful applicants will not necessarily receive individual notifications. However, important announcements and future submission opportunities are expected to be shared through official channels. When Will Successful Applicants Be Notified? Successful applicants are expected to be contacted by mid-December 2026 . Applicants should ensure that they provide accurate contact information when completing their submission. They should also monitor their email and official programme communication channels after submitting their proposal. How Will Winners Be Selected? The evaluation process and selection criteria are outlined in the official Terms and Conditions document. Applicants are encouraged to review the Terms and Conditions carefully before submitting their proposals. Understanding the evaluation criteria can help entrepreneurs prepare stronger applications and ensure that their submissions align with the expectations of the programme. A competitive proposal should generally demonstrate: Innovation Practicality Business viability Investment potential Clear revenue generation Climate-smart practices Resilience Relevance to the value chain Realistic capital requirements Potential for growth and impact Applicants should focus on clearly communicating why their idea matters and how it can realistically be implemented. What Value Chains Are Eligible? For the e-MOVE Call for Proposals, applicants should focus on the cashew value chain . The broader programme information also references opportunities connected to other value chains under the Agribusiness e-Academy, including: Maize Livestock, including cattle, sheep and goats Cocoa However, applicants should carefully follow the requirements of the specific submission window and programme pathway they are applying under. Ideas submitted outside the eligible value chains may not be considered. For this particular e-MOVE opportunity, applicants should ensure that their proposal clearly demonstrates a connection to the cashew sector . Who Is Organising the Competition? The competition is organised by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH through initiatives including: The Agri-Business Facility for Africa (ABF) Market-Oriented Value Chains for Jobs and Growth in the ECOWAS Region (MOVE-ComCashew) Both initiatives are part of German Development Cooperation. The projects contribute to the Joint Action: Business Support Facility for Resilient Agricultural Value Chains The Joint Action brings together several development partners and institutions, including: The European Union Directorate-General for International Partnerships (INTPA) The Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS) The German Government The Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) The initiative is jointly co-financed by the European Union under the Samoa Agreement with OACPS and by BMZ, with implementation support provided by GIZ. Important Things to Remember Before Applying Before submitting an application, candidates should carefully check that they have completed all requirements. Here is a useful application checklist: Eligibility Checklist You are at least 18 years old You are based in an eligible OACPS member state You have an innovative idea connected to the cashew value chain You are interested in developing a climate-smart agribusiness venture Training Checklist You have registered on the e-MOVE or atingi platform You have completed Introduction to Conservation Agriculture You have completed Creating an Investment-Ready Agribusiness You have obtained a valid certificate ID from the required final course Submission Checklist You have developed a complete AgriCanvas Your idea focuses on the eligible cashew value chain You have explained the climate-smart or resilience component You have developed a clear revenue model You have estimated your capital requirements You have entered your AgriCanvas directly into the official form You have reviewed all responses before submitting You have submitted before the deadline Tips for Preparing a Strong AgriCanvas Submission Applicants should approach the competition as an opportunity to develop a real business concept rather than simply filling out an application form. Here are several tips that may help strengthen a proposal. 1. Identify a Real Problem Strong business ideas often begin with a clearly identified problem. Think about challenges within the cashew value chain that affect: Farmers Processors Traders Consumers Exporters Rural communities Your proposed solution should demonstrate how it addresses a specific need. 2. Be Specific About Your Customers Clearly identify who will benefit from or purchase your product or service. Avoid describing your target market too broadly. Instead, consider specific customer groups and their needs. 3. Develop a Realistic Revenue Model Explain exactly how the business will generate income. An innovative idea is important, but a sustainable business must also have a clear path toward financial viability. 4. Integrate Climate-Smart Solutions Think carefully about how your project can contribute to environmental sustainability and resilience. Do not treat the climate-smart component as an afterthought. Instead, integrate it directly into your business model. 5. Make Realistic Financial Estimates Your capital requirements should be reasonable and connected to the actual needs of your proposed venture. Avoid unrealistic figures or estimates that cannot be explained. 6. Demonstrate Innovation Innovation does not necessarily mean inventing an entirely new product. Innovation can involve improving an existing process, introducing new technology, developing a better business model or adapting a successful solution to a new market. 7. Review Your Application Before Submission Before submitting, carefully check: Spelling and grammar Certificate information Business model details Revenue projections Climate-smart components Capital estimates Completeness of responses A well-organised and clearly written submission can make it easier for evaluators to understand your idea. APPLY HERE Deadline The deadline for submitting proposals under Submission Window 3 is: 30 October 2026 Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin the required courses and develop their AgriCanvas early. Since completion of the mandatory training is required before submitting an idea, waiting until the final days of the submission window may create unnecessary pressure. Starting early gives applicants sufficient time to: Complete both mandatory courses. Understand the learning materials. Develop a strong business idea. Build a detailed AgriCanvas. Refine the revenue model. Identify climate-smart components. Estimate capital requirements. Review the final application. Submit before the deadline. How to Apply Interested and eligible applicants should begin by accessing the e-MOVE learning pathway, completing the mandatory courses and preparing their AgriCanvas. Applicants can access the programme resources through the official platforms. Visit HERE to learn more about the Call for Proposals 2026. Conclusion The e-MOVE Call for Proposals 2026: Build Your AgriCanvas. Build Your Future provides an important opportunity for young and emerging entrepreneurs to transform innovative cashew sector ideas into structured, investment-ready and climate-smart business ventures. Beyond the possibility of receiving EUR 2,000 in direct funding or valuable business equipment , participants benefit from free agricultural and entrepreneurship training that can help them develop practical skills for building sustainable enterprises. The programme is particularly valuable because it encourages applicants to think beyond an initial idea. Participants must consider how their businesses will generate revenue, respond to climate challenges, attract investment and contribute to resilient agricultural value chains. For aspiring agripreneurs across eligible OACPS member states, this Call for Proposals presents an opportunity to combine learning, innovation and entrepreneurship while contributing to the future of the cashew industry. Eligible applicants should begin the mandatory e-MOVE courses as early as possible, carefully develop their AgriCanvas and ensure their final submission is completed before the 30 October 2026 deadline . title: Airbus Global Graduate Programme 2027: Graduate Satellite AIT Electrical Engineer Opportunity in the UK
summary: Applications are now open for the Airbus Global Graduate Programme 2027 , offering an exciting opportunity for a recently graduated engineer to begin a career as a Satellite Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) Electrical Engineer in Stevenage, United Kingdom. The position is designed for graduates who want to work at the intersection of electrical engineering, spacecraft systems, software, testing and the space industry . Successful candidates will join Airbus Defence and Space and participate in a structured two-year graduate development journey beginning in September 2027. Rather than simply offering an entry-level position, Airbus describes the programme as a development pathway intended to build technical expertise, business understanding, communication skills and future leadership capabilities. The successful graduate will receive practical exposure to spacecraft integration and testing while contributing to projects connected to major space missions. About the Airbus Global Graduate Programme 2027 The Airbus Global Graduate Programme is designed to help recent university graduates transition from academic study into professional careers within one of the world s leading aerospace organisations. The programme combines practical employment with structured professional development. Graduates are expected to become productive members of their teams from the beginning while receiving support to strengthen their technical, interpersonal and leadership capabilities. According to the vacancy, the two-year development journey includes areas such as: Inclusive leadership Airbus values Resilience Communication Emotional intelligence Business understanding Technical development Professional collaboration Leadership preparation Graduates will also become part of a global graduate community and participate in an annual in-person development week. This provides opportunities to meet fellow graduates, interact with experienced Airbus leaders and learn more about the wider organisation. The programme is therefore particularly suitable for candidates looking for more than their first job and who want a structured route into a long-term aerospace career. Graduate Satellite AIT Electrical Engineer Role The successful candidate will follow a development pathway toward becoming a Satellite Assembly, Integration and Test Electrical Engineer . Satellite AIT is a critical part of spacecraft development. Before a spacecraft can be launched, its systems and subsystems must be assembled, integrated, tested and verified to ensure they work correctly and meet the required technical specifications. In this role, the graduate can expect to gain exposure to a broad range of spacecraft subsystems and learn how the Satellite Assembly Integration and Test department operates. Airbus highlights experience with major European space missions, including: Solar Orbiter BIOMASS ExoMars Rover The organisation is also involved in projects relating to secure space communications for the UK Government. This means the graduate could gain exposure to highly specialised work involving spacecraft technologies, testing processes and systems used in major space programmes. What Will You Do? The role provides exposure to both electrical engineering and software-related activities , making it particularly interesting for graduates who have interdisciplinary interests. Responsibilities and development activities may include: 1. Spacecraft subsystem integration The graduate will learn how different spacecraft subsystems are integrated into a functioning spacecraft. This involves understanding how individual systems interact and ensuring that the interfaces between components operate as intended. 2. Functional and system testing Testing is a major part of the position. The graduate will develop knowledge of spacecraft functional and system-level testing. This may involve: Conducting electrical measurements Running test procedures Analysing test results Identifying unexpected behaviour Supporting troubleshooting activities Documenting test outcomes 3. Anomaly investigation Spacecraft testing can reveal unexpected results or technical anomalies. The graduate will develop skills in investigating these issues and determining their possible causes. This requires analytical thinking, attention to detail and the ability to make evidence-based decisions. 4. Programming and scripting The role also offers opportunities to strengthen software and automation skills. Airbus specifically mentions the use of: C-based programming languages Java Bash scripting Other scripting tools Candidates with programming experience or a strong interest in developing their programming capabilities may therefore find this role particularly relevant. 5. Test documentation and reporting Accurate documentation is essential in aerospace engineering. The successful candidate will be expected to learn how to: Record test results Prepare technical documentation Produce clear reports Communicate technical information Prepare presentations Maintain accurate records of engineering activities 6. Environmental testing The graduate may support environmental test campaigns designed to assess spacecraft performance under conditions relevant to launch and operation. This can provide valuable experience in understanding how spacecraft systems are verified before deployment. 7. Launch-site activities The role may also involve supporting spacecraft interface checks at launch sites. Because Airbus states that the organisation supports spacecraft launches and environmental test campaigns, the position may involve overseas travel . This can provide graduates with international exposure and an opportunity to understand how spacecraft move from development and testing toward launch. Rotational Placement An important feature of the graduate programme is the opportunity to undertake at least one rotational placement . The rotation is intended to broaden the graduate s experience and support development toward the eventual Satellite AIT Electrical Engineer position. This can help the successful candidate understand different aspects of Airbus operations while developing a broader professional perspective. Skills and Qualifications Required Applicants should have a degree or equivalent qualification in a relevant engineering discipline. Airbus identifies the following academic backgrounds as suitable: Electronics Engineering Electrical Systems Engineering Avionics Engineering Space Engineering Similar engineering disciplines Applicants should also be recent graduates or have first professional experience in engineering . In addition to academic qualifications, Airbus is looking for candidates who demonstrate strong communication, teamwork and personal-development capabilities. Technical Skills and Experience Candidates are expected to demonstrate an interest or experience in practical engineering applications. The vacancy highlights several areas that may strengthen an application. Engineering knowledge Applicants should demonstrate a strong interest in applying engineering knowledge practically rather than relying exclusively on theoretical understanding. Programming and scripting Knowledge of programming and scripting is desirable, particularly experience with technologies such as: C Java Bash scripting Other programming or scripting languages Candidates should be prepared to explain how they have applied these skills through university projects, personal projects, internships, employment or other technical activities. Problem-solving The position requires graduates who enjoy identifying solutions to technically complex problems. Applicants should demonstrate an ability to: Analyse problems logically Investigate anomalies Evaluate evidence Develop practical solutions Make informed decisions Communication Strong written and verbal communication skills are important because the engineer will need to work with technical teams and communicate engineering information clearly. Applicants should be able to: Listen carefully Understand technical information Explain information clearly Prepare accurate documentation Communicate effectively with colleagues Teamwork Airbus is looking for graduates who can work collaboratively in a technical environment. A positive, proactive and reliable approach is important, particularly because spacecraft development involves multidisciplinary teams working toward common objectives. Personal Qualities Airbus Is Looking For Beyond technical qualifications, successful candidates should demonstrate several professional qualities. These include: A proactive, can-do attitude Reliability Teamwork Self-awareness Curiosity Creativity Strong communication Willingness to learn Interest in technical problem-solving Evidence-based decision-making Desire for continuous development Ability to work in an open and trusting environment Airbus also places emphasis on candidates taking responsibility for their own development. Therefore, applicants should demonstrate not only what they already know but also how they intend to continue learning and improving. Why This Graduate Opportunity Is Significant The Airbus Global Graduate Programme provides several advantages for someone starting a career in aerospace. Structured professional development Instead of being left to navigate an entry-level position independently, graduates receive a structured two-year development programme. Aerospace industry experience The role provides an opportunity to work directly with spacecraft-related engineering activities. Exposure to major space programmes The vacancy references missions including Solar Orbiter, BIOMASS and ExoMars Rover, providing an indication of the scale and technical significance of projects associated with the organisation. Technical and software development The position combines electrical engineering with software and scripting, allowing graduates to develop interdisciplinary capabilities. International exposure The role may involve overseas travel in connection with environmental testing and spacecraft launches. Leadership development The programme includes training intended to develop future leadership capabilities. Global graduate network Participants will join a global graduate community and have opportunities to interact with graduates and experienced Airbus leaders. Potential long-term career development At the conclusion of the two-year programme, the graduate is expected to have developed into the position of Satellite AIT Electrical Engineer . This makes the programme particularly attractive to candidates who want to build a long-term career in aerospace rather than simply obtain short-term graduate employment. Recruitment and Selection Process Airbus outlines a multi-stage recruitment process for the opportunity. The process is expected to follow these stages: Online application Online task-based assessment Application review Virtual assessment centre Offer The application will initially be reviewed by the Talent Acquisition Partner and hiring manager. Candidates who progress through the process should therefore be prepared to demonstrate both their technical capabilities and their suitability for Airbus working environment. Application Deadline The official application deadline is: 30 September 2026 However, applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications early. Airbus specifically warns that some roles may close before the stated deadline if a sufficient number of applications are received. Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final day. Important Visa and Work-Eligibility Information One of the most important considerations for international applicants is the position s work-authorisation requirement. Airbus states that it cannot provide Skilled Worker visa sponsorship for this position . The company welcomes applications from candidates who already have the right to work in the United Kingdom or who qualify to work through other available routes, such as the: Graduate Visa Youth Mobility Scheme Other eligible immigration routes Applicants should independently verify their eligibility under current UK immigration requirements before applying. For detailed and official immigration information, candidates should consult UK Visas and Immigration. Application Documents Applications and CVs must be submitted in English . Applicants should therefore ensure that their CV clearly presents: Their relevant engineering degree Technical skills Programming experience Engineering projects Practical experience Relevant internships or work experience Teamwork experience Problem-solving abilities Communication skills Academic or personal projects relevant to aerospace or engineering Where possible, candidates should demonstrate achievements rather than simply listing skills. For example, instead of stating that they have programming skills, an applicant could describe a university or personal project where they used C, Java, Bash or another language to solve a specific engineering problem. How to Strengthen Your Application Because Airbus asks applicants to submit only one application to the Airbus Global Graduate Programme , candidates should carefully select the opportunity that best matches their background. Before submitting your application, consider the following: 1. Tailor your CV Make the most relevant engineering, programming and practical experience easy for the recruiter to identify. 2. Highlight practical projects University projects, engineering laboratories, programming projects, robotics projects, electronics projects and other hands-on experiences can help demonstrate practical ability. 3. Demonstrate problem-solving Use examples that show how you identified a problem, analysed it and developed a solution. 4. Explain your interest in aerospace A strong application should make it clear why you want to work in aerospace and why spacecraft AIT interests you. 5. Show interdisciplinary skills Because the role combines electrical engineering, spacecraft systems and software, applicants should highlight experience across multiple technical areas where applicable. 6. Demonstrate teamwork Spacecraft development is highly collaborative. Include examples showing your ability to work effectively with others. 7. Prepare for the assessment Since the recruitment process includes an online task-based assessment and virtual assessment centre, applicants should be prepared to demonstrate analytical thinking, communication and problem-solving skills. 8. Submit early Although the deadline is 30 September 2026, some positions may close earlier because of application volume. Accessibility and Inclusion Airbus states that applicants can request adjustments during the recruitment process. Examples may include: Accessible facilities Additional time for written exercises Other reasonable adjustments Candidates who require an adjustment are encouraged to communicate their needs to Airbus. The company states that information disclosed for this purpose will be treated confidentially. Airbus also states its commitment to workforce diversity and an inclusive working environment and welcomes applications irrespective of factors including social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief. Who Can Apply? Category of people who qualify This opportunity is primarily intended for: Recent university graduates Early-career engineering professionals Candidates with a degree or equivalent qualification in Electronics, Electrical Systems, Avionics, Space Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline Candidates with an interest in spacecraft systems, electrical engineering, software, testing and aerospace Candidates with strong English communication skills Candidates who can demonstrate teamwork, problem-solving and practical engineering abilities Candidates who are legally entitled to work in the UK through an existing or eligible route Nationality and geographic eligibility Airbus describes its Global Graduate Programme as seeking talented graduates from around the globe . However, this specific Satellite AIT Electrical Engineer position is based in Stevenage, United Kingdom , and Airbus states that Skilled Worker visa sponsorship is not available . Therefore, international applicants should not assume that being eligible to apply automatically means they are eligible to work in the UK. Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions may consider the opportunity if they independently meet the position s work-authorisation requirements. The key issue for candidates outside the UK is therefore existing or otherwise eligible UK work rights , rather than nationality alone. Application Link Interested candidates should review the complete vacancy requirements and submit their application through the official Airbus careers platform. Application deadline: 30 September 2026 Candidates can also review Airbus recruitment guidance and application tips through Airbus Careers Recruitment Process Tips. APPLY HERE About Airbus Airbus is a major aerospace company operating across commercial aircraft, defence and security, helicopters and space. The organisation describes its purpose around pioneering sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. Its activities span technologically advanced aircraft, defence and security systems, connected services and space programmes. For graduates interested in aerospace engineering, working at Airbus can provide exposure to complex international projects and multidisciplinary engineering environments. Visit HERE to learn more about Airbus Global Graduate Programme 2027. Final Thoughts The Airbus Global Graduate Programme 2027 – Graduate Satellite AIT Electrical Engineer position represents a strong opportunity for recent engineering graduates who want to establish themselves in the aerospace and space sector. The two-year programme combines employment with structured technical and professional development, giving graduates the opportunity to gain practical experience in spacecraft assembly, integration and testing while strengthening their electrical engineering, programming, problem-solving and communication capabilities. The opportunity is particularly relevant to graduates with backgrounds in electronics, electrical systems, avionics, space engineering or related disciplines , especially those who have practical engineering experience and an interest in programming and spacecraft technology. However, applicants should pay close attention to the UK work-authorisation requirement , as Airbus has explicitly stated that Skilled Worker visa sponsorship is not available for this position. With applications closing on 30 September 2026 , eligible candidates should prepare their English-language CV carefully, tailor their application to the role and submit well before the deadline, as Airbus notes that individual opportunities may close earlier if application numbers are high.
